before: A discriminated union has a shared field whose literal value identifies each variant.
After a branch handles one variant, TypeScript can narrow the remaining possibilities.
never means no value can remain at that point under the declared type. Passing a remaining variant to a function expecting never produces a compiler error.

For the exercise, return "Waiting", "Ready: title", or "Failed: reason". Finish the switch with assertNever(notice). If a new variant is added later, the compiler should point to the missing handling.

The new-case check temporarily extends Notice in a separate compilation. A complete strict-return switch or another supported exhaustive handler can satisfy this behavior without copying one helper spelling.
after: A discriminated union uses a shared label, such as kind, to identify each possible shape.
When a branch handles one shape and returns, that shape is no longer possible on the remaining path.
A switch selects a branch by its value. Each case below returns text for one signal kind.
Never is a type with no possible value. At the end of a fully handled choice, nothing should remain. Passing a still-possible shape to a never parameter causes a type error.
For the project, return Waiting, Ready: followed by the title, or Failed: followed by the reason. Keep a space after each colon. Handle every notice kind.

The checks add a new notice kind in a separate copy to see whether missing handling causes an error. Keep the final never check or another complete checked approach. Do not use a cast to hide the missing case.

before.question: A new {kind:"cancelled"} variant is added to Notice but not to the switch. Why should assertNever(notice) fail compilation?
choices: notice can still be cancelled there, so it is not never
never automatically adds a cancelled branch
The compiler runs the network request and sees cancellation
before.explanation: The unhandled variant remains possible at the end. That value cannot be passed to a never parameter, revealing the missing case before execution.

after.question: A cancelled kind is added but not handled. Why does assertNever(notice) cause a type error?
choices: Notice could still be cancelled there, so it is not never
The compiler runs a request and observes cancellation
after.explanation: The unhandled shape is still possible. It cannot be passed to a type with no possible values.

changes.before: Deepens previously brief never usage with compile-negative changed-union verification. Starter intentionally fails strict compilation until missing cases are handled. No as never escape hatch; runtime checks alone cannot prove exhaustiveness.
changes.after: The starter reports a type error until all cases are handled. The helper can throw for unexpected running data, but outside data still needs its own checks.
